label: r3c1
name: flip + 64 envs (more updates)
hypothesis: Same network as r2c2, but n_envs drops 128 to 64 with 16 minibatches of 64 samples. That gives about 120 updates instead of 60 on the same number of samples. r2c2 was still improving and doubling updates gave +14 points, so learning looks limited by updates. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is not above 0.888 by more than about 0.03, or if the seeds diverge, since updates on fewer environments are noisier.
last_analysis: The main gain came from flipping the feature map along x so that each anchor logit pools over the cells the brick actually fills. Without it, dev success was 0, and learning the mapping with axial mixing (r1c3) also scored 0. After that fix, the number of updates mattered most. With the same sample budget, dev success went from 0.745 (30 updates) to 0.888 (60) to 0.931 (about 120, n_envs 64), and both seeds of each run stayed close. Changes that cost samples or added instability did not help: the footprint-conv head (about equal), the dilated third conv (0.851) and lr 2e-3 (0.833). Seed noise looks like roughly ±0.03–0.05. The remaining failures are small: IoU is 0.995 and about 0.12 cells per episode land outside the target. n_envs is already at its minimum of 64, so this round halves rollout_len to 8 to double the updates again. It also tests trading one PPO epoch for more samples, and a lower entropy bonus, since evaluation is greedy.
